en.title: Obsession Director Curry Barker Lands Massive Eight-Figure Universal Deal
en.summary: Fresh off the unexpected box office dominance of his horror hit Obsession, director Curry Barker has secured a monumental eight-figure deal with Universal for his next project. This move solidifies Barker's rapid ascent from YouTube creator to Hollywood powerhouse.
en.body:
The meteoric rise of **Curry Barker** continues unabated. Following the phenomenal box office success of his independent horror film **Obsession**, Universal Pictures is wasting no time in doubling down on the 26-year-old director. Reports confirm an eight-figure deal has been inked, ensuring Barker's next studio feature will be financed and distributed by the major studio. This is a significant testament to the impact **Obsession** has had, not just with audiences but also in Hollywood boardrooms.

Barker’s journey to this point is a compelling narrative in itself. He first gained traction on YouTube, eventually releasing a feature-length found footage film, **Milk And Serial**, on the platform in 2024. After struggling to find traditional distribution, the passionate fan reception to **Milk And Serial** helped secure independent funding for **Obsession**. The film's strong debut at TIFF in 2025 caught the eye of Focus Features, a subsidiary of Universal, which subsequently acquired distribution rights. **Obsession** itself has proven to be a remarkably shrewd investment, reportedly made for less than a million dollars, and its box office performance has far exceeded expectations, even outperforming established franchises like *The Mandalorian and Grogu*.

## The New Horror Darling

Barker's success is being viewed by many in the industry as a watershed moment, particularly alongside fellow YouTube alum **Kane Parsons** and his film **Backrooms**. Both directors are proving that fresh, digitally-native perspectives can challenge and even surpass the box office might of established franchises. Universal’s swift action with Barker suggests they recognize this potent combination of raw talent and audience connection. He will be reteaming with **Blumhouse Atomic Monster** and **Universal Film Group** for his upcoming project, a partnership that has clearly been fruitful. Barker expressed his enthusiasm, noting, "This film is something I’ve been excited to make for a while, and I’m thrilled to be reteaming with Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Universal Film Group for it."

## What This Means for Fans

For fans of Barker's distinctive, high-energy horror, this deal is fantastic news. It means more original content from a director who has quickly established a unique voice. The substantial investment from Universal indicates a strong belief in Barker's ability to deliver commercially successful and artistically engaging films. This isn't just about one director; it signifies a potential opening for other emerging filmmakers who have cultivated audiences online. The success of **Obsession** and **Backrooms** might just pave the way for a new generation of genre filmmakers to break through in a major way, offering fresh scares and compelling narratives that resonate with modern audiences.

## What's Next

Details surrounding Barker's next untitled project are still emerging, but the eight-figure deal suggests a significant scope. Fans can anticipate further announcements regarding the film’s premise and production timeline in the coming months as Universal and Blumhouse gear up for what is sure to be another highly anticipated release.

content_raw: 2026 is turning out to be a phenomenally good year for horror directors who got their start on YouTube, as Curry Barker’s  Obsession   joins Kane Parsons’  Backrooms   in cheerfully kicking the shit out of more established franchises and filmmakers at the box office. (Both movies have managed to beat The Mandalorian And Grogu   with their domestic takes, for instance, while Barker’s film will be running neck-and-neck with Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day   to see who comes in second to  Toy Story 5  this weekend.) None of which has missed the notice of Barker’s partners at Universal, who have now tossed a reported eight-figure deal at the 26-year-old director for his next film. To be clear, this deal is in connection to Barker’s third  studio film; he already worked with Universal-owned Focus Features to make his second studio movie, Anything But Ghosts , back before Obsession  started delivering its “Oh shit, that’s a better than 300-to-1” return on investment. (Barker also previously released a feature-length found footage movie, Milk And Serial , on YouTube in 2024, after struggling to find distribution for the movie; the fevered fan reception to the movie helped secure independent funding for Obsession, with Focus buying in on after the film had a strong opening at TIFF in 2025.) As with his previous films, Barker will be making the untitled movie in association with Blumhouse, releasing a (slightly vague) statement this weekend in which he praised the horror studio. “This film is something I’ve been excited to make for a while,” Barker noted, “And I’m thrilled to be reteaming with Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Universal Film Group for it. They’ve built the kind of home for bold, original storytelling that every filmmaker dreams of, and I couldn’t imagine better collaborators for this film.” No plot details for the movie are being even vaguely hinted at, beyond it being an “original horror idea” disconnected from Barker’s earlier work. (Meanwhile, he’s also supposedly on the hook to make a new  Texas Chainsaw Massacre  movie for A24, although it’s currently unclear how that’s going to fit into Barker’s increasingly busy schedule.)
